_comment: Targeted RFI review benchmark. Each case is an RFI a person really issued, used ONLY as the expected OUTPUT: the review never sees it.
A case passes when one candidate of the run matches every field of an expected finding. `pairs` are grid names or values that must appear as 'a = b' in either order;
`sheets` must each be named in the finding's evidence. Candidates matching no expected finding are listed, never scored as wrong: the sheets may carry real problems nobody wrote an RFI for.
Run: python benchmarks/rfi_eval.py --run <review run id> [--case rfi-002] with DATABASE_URL set.

cases.source: BIM RFI 002 'CONFIRM THE GRID LAYOUT': 'Please confirm the correct grid layout, as a mismatch has been observed between the Architectural and Structural drawings.'

expected.what: The same grid lines are named differently on the structural and the architectural plan

cases.source: BIM RFI 015 'Discrepancies in dimensions and column location' (A3.27, A3.35): 'Please clarify the correct column locations and intended markings so the model can be updated accurately for further coordination and development.' Markup: the columns along one wall line of the Level 14 enlarged plan (A3.35, 1/4") do not sit where the Level 14 overall plan (A3.27, 1/8") shows them.
cases.knownGap: Not findable from these two sheets, and correctly so. Laid over each other by the column overlay (plan_match), A3.35 and A3.27 AGREE: detail 1 matches 4 columns and detail 2 matches 5, with no difference except a column the enlarged detail's window cuts off. The RFI's green boxes are the author's own markup (Square annotations) showing where the LEVEL BELOW puts its columns, which neither sheet carries. The case becomes findable when the level-13 plan is in the project: the same overlay at a 1:1 ratio reports level-14 columns that do not stack on level-13 ones.

expected.what: Column locations along the Level 14 wall line differ between the enlarged plan and the overall plan

cases.needs: The Level 13 plan (the level below), compared with A3.27 at the same scale.
